title: About CBS
paragraphs: Chronological Bible Storying (CBS) is an exciting tool being used in evangelism, discipleship, and church planting among primary oral learners around the world, including many unreached people groups. CBS training methodology has been increasingly developed and improved over the last few decades through work of organizations such as New Tribes Missions, the International Mission Board, and others. While CBS has become prominent in the world of missions as an intentional method of evangelism and discipleship, it is actually as old as biblical history. Our sovereign God decreed that the historical events of the Bible occur in a certain order and decreed that people remember them in stories that were not only written down, but also passed down from generation to generation by mouth. These stories, starting with the story of Creation and extending all the way through the stories of Jesus and the early church, have become for us a clear history of almighty God working out his plan to bring redemption to a sinful, broken world. And even as God was working through history so that we might be saved and live in a growing relationship with him, he was also through His stories teaching mankind all along the way all about Himself, about man, and about how sinful man may be restored into relationship with that merciful God.
To see God's people and their leaders in East Africa understanding, being transformed by, and communicating the Gospel of grace to one another and to the world.
Clearly teaching biblical truth and communicating the Gospel of grace through God's stories shared through oral methodology and equipping and motivating believers to do the same.

It is chronological . Instead of taking quick shortcuts to present the Gospel message, CBS teaches the Gospel in a much slower, fuller way that is particularly valuable in long term relational evangelism and discipleship. CBS involves teaching through Bible stories in chronological order, beginning with Creation and continuing to the stories of Jesus. By doing this we lay a firm foundation of who God is, who man is, and how God wants to relate with men. In CBS, one might use 30 to 45 Bible stories which are key to the redemption message, all presented in the same order in which we find them in Scripture.

It is Bible. It is not simply using stories from our lives to illustrate the message of our sermons. It is not even simply using Bible stories for illustration only. It involves telling the Bible stories accurately and teaching the main principles of redemption found in these stories.

It is storytelling. Storytelling as a method of communicating the Gospel and biblical truth is very valuable in the African setting because Africans are story tellers. Most of the crucial truth and wisdom that passes down from generation to generation is communicated in an oral method – through stories, songs, proverbs, and ritual in the context of community – rather than through books and note taking. Primary oral learners prefer to learn the most important things in life through story. Stories help abstract truths become concrete and applicable in every day lives. In ever lesson, a Bible story is the vehicle that carries the biblical teaching. Because stories are naturally interesting, such lessons hold people's interest. As they learn the stories by heart learners are able to easily reproduce them and communicate gospel truths to others. While simply reading stories from the Bible and teaching about them verse by verse can be very instructive, it is often even more effective when the learner knows the story by heart and is able to tell it in its entirety with feeling and persuasion and then begin a simple dialogue through helpful character based questions. )
